plants.name: Begonia rex 'Escargot'
plants.tip: Water the compost, never the leaves. Wet foliage in still air is how powdery mildew starts.
plants.colour: Silver and olive spiral, edged in maroon and covered in fine hairs

plants.name: Begonia rex 'Fireworks'
plants.tip: Keep it out of draughts. Sudden cold air, not dry compost, is what strips the leaves in winter.
plants.colour: Silver leaf with a deep purple centre and purple radiating veins

plants.name: Begonia rex 'Silver Limbo'
plants.tip: Small enough for a terrarium. Let the top two centimetres dry before you water it again.
plants.colour: Small silver-blue leaves flecked and edged with dark green

plants.name: Begonia rex 'Red Kiss'
plants.tip: A dark leaf still needs bright indirect light. In a dim spot the red band loses its contrast.
plants.colour: Near-black leaf with a broad rose-red band inside the margin

plants.name: Begonia rex 'Inca Flame'
plants.tip: Rex begonias go dormant if they get cold. Hold back the water and it will releaf in spring.
plants.colour: Orange-red leaf overlaid with silver and a dark centre

plants.name: Begonia rex 'Jurassic Silver Swirl'
plants.tip: Sturdier than the older rex types, but it still rots if the pot is left standing in water.
plants.colour: Broad silver leaf with a dark green swirl around the centre

plants.name: Begonia rex 'Salsa'
plants.tip: Pinch the flower stems off as they appear. They take energy from the leaves and are barely worth having.
plants.colour: Red centre spreading into a silver and green outer margin

plants.name: Begonia 'Benitochiba'
plants.tip: Grows from a surface rhizome. Bury it and it rots, so let it sit on top of the compost.
plants.colour: Deeply lobed silver leaf with purple-red veins and margin

plants.name: Begonia masoniana (iron cross begonia)
plants.tip: The bristly leaves hold droplets and mark. Water at the base and keep the air moving.
plants.colour: Puckered apple-green leaf with a dark brown cross at the centre

plants.name: Begonia masoniana 'River'
plants.tip: Wants humidity above average. A pebble tray or a closed case does more for it than misting.
plants.colour: Quilted bronze-green leaf with silver netting between the veins

plants.name: Begonia bowerae (eyelash begonia)
plants.tip: Shallow-rooted, so it prefers a wide shallow pot to a deep one and dislikes sitting wet.
plants.colour: Small bright green leaf edged with dark stitching and white hairs

plants.name: Begonia bowerae 'Tiger Paws'
plants.tip: Leaf edges crisp in dry air, so keep it well away from a radiator over winter.
plants.colour: Lime-green leaf marbled with chocolate-brown and fringed with pale hairs

plants.name: Begonia 'Cleopatra'
plants.tip: Hard sun bleaches the bronze out to yellow. Bright indirect light keeps the contrast.
plants.colour: Star-shaped leaf in bronze and gold, red on the underside

plants.name: Begonia 'Erythrophylla' (beefsteak begonia)
plants.tip: One of the toughest begonias. It forgives a missed watering far better than a soggy pot.
plants.colour: Round glossy olive leaves with deep red undersides

plants.name: Begonia 'Marmaduke'
plants.tip: The large leaves are brittle. Site it where nothing brushes past, as a snapped leaf does not regrow.
plants.colour: Large chartreuse leaf spotted and splashed with chocolate-brown

plants.name: Begonia soli-mutata
plants.tip: Leaf colour tracks the light it gets, so after a move expect the new growth to look different.
plants.colour: Puckered leaf shifting from olive-green to bronze in brighter light

plants.name: Begonia goegoensis (fire king begonia)
plants.tip: A jungle species that sulks in average room air. A bathroom or a closed case suits it better.
plants.colour: Round bronze-green peltate leaf with a network of pale veins

plants.name: Begonia rajah
plants.tip: Needs steady warmth and humidity. Cold nights are what kill it, not a dry week.
plants.colour: Small puckered chocolate leaf with bright green veining

plants.name: Begonia pavonina (peacock begonia)
plants.tip: The blue sheen is an adaptation to deep shade, so bright light washes it out.
plants.colour: Dark green leaf with a blue iridescent sheen in low light

plants.name: Begonia carolineifolia
plants.tip: The thick rhizome stores water, so it takes a dry spell far better than a wet one.
plants.colour: Fans of glossy mid-green leaflets on a stout upright rhizome

plants.name: Begonia maculata 'Wightii'
plants.tip: It grows tall and topples. Cut it back hard each spring and root the cuttings in water.
plants.colour: Olive wing-shaped leaf with silver-white spots, deep red beneath

plants.name: Begonia listada
plants.tip: Bright indirect light and no draughts. It sheds leaves when the air around it dries out.
plants.colour: Dark velvety leaf with a single lime stripe down the centre

plants.name: Begonia serratipetala
plants.tip: The pink flecking is strongest on new growth in good light. Older leaves settle to plain bronze.
plants.colour: Bronze-green saw-edged leaf flecked with pink

plants.name: Begonia amphioxus
plants.tip: A Borneo species for a terrarium. Ordinary room humidity is not enough to keep it going.
plants.colour: Narrow green leaf spotted red, with a red tip at each end

plants.name: Begonia luxurians (palm leaf begonia)
plants.tip: It needs room and light to build the full palm-like leaves. Cramped, it stays leggy and sparse.
plants.colour: Fans of narrow green leaflets held on tall red stems

plants.name: Begonia venosa
plants.tip: The felted leaves hold water and rot. Water the compost only, and give it more light than most begonias.
plants.colour: Thick felted grey-white leaves on a stout upright stem

plants.name: Begonia 'Gryphon'
plants.tip: Vigorous for a begonia and grown purely for the leaves. Pot it on each spring or growth stalls.
plants.colour: Large lobed leaves in deep green with silver between the veins

plants.name: Begonia 'Lucerna'
plants.tip: Cane begonias flower on mature growth, so never cut every stem back in the same year.
plants.colour: Silver-spotted olive leaves, red beneath, with pendent pink flower clusters

plants.name: Begonia 'Sophie Cecile'
plants.tip: Stake the canes early. Once a stem has leaned it will not straighten again.
plants.colour: Large silver-spotted leaves with cut edges and pink flower clusters

plants.name: Begonia coccinea (angel wing begonia)
plants.tip: It flowers best slightly pot-bound, so resist moving it up a pot size too soon.
plants.colour: Glossy green wing-shaped leaves with red margins and coral flowers

plants.name: Begonia 'Tamaya'
plants.tip: Sold as a standard on a single trunk. Rub out the shoots at the base or it reverts to a bush.
plants.colour: Silver-spotted olive leaves on one thick trunk, with pink flowers

plants.name: Begonia 'Dragon Wing Red'
plants.tip: Bred to take heat and rain outdoors. It sheds spent flowers itself, so deadheading is wasted effort.
plants.colour: Glossy deep green wing-shaped leaves with red flower clusters

plants.name: Begonia 'Dragon Wing Pink'
plants.tip: Feed it fortnightly right through summer, or the flowering thins out by late August.
plants.colour: Glossy deep green leaves with clear pink flower clusters

plants.name: Begonia boliviensis
plants.tip: Tuberous, so it dies back for winter. Keep the tuber dry and frost-free until spring.
plants.colour: Narrow toothed leaves with pendent orange-red flowers

plants.name: Begonia 'Bonfire'
plants.tip: Best in a hanging basket where the stems can arch. Let the top of the compost dry between waterings.
plants.colour: Arching stems of narrow leaves with fiery orange-red flowers

plants.name: Begonia x tuberhybrida (tuberous begonia)
plants.tip: Start the tubers hollow side up in spring. Planted the wrong way up they rot before they shoot.
plants.colour: Large double flowers in red, orange, yellow, pink or white

plants.name: Begonia 'Nonstop'
plants.tip: Bred to flower without a rest, but it still needs deadheading to carry on into autumn.
plants.colour: Compact plants with double flowers in warm reds, oranges and yellows

plants.name: Begonia x hiemalis (Rieger begonia)
plants.tip: Sold in full flower and usually thrown away after. Cut it back instead and it flowers again.
plants.colour: Glossy dark green leaves with double flowers in red, orange or pink

plants.name: Begonia semperflorens (wax begonia)
plants.tip: The bronze-leaved forms take full sun; the green-leaved ones scorch and want some shade.
plants.colour: Waxy green or bronze leaves with small pink, red or white flowers

plants.name: Begonia grandis (hardy begonia)
plants.tip: The one begonia that comes through a British winter outdoors. It dies back and returns in late spring.
plants.colour: Olive leaves with red veins and undersides, sprays of pale pink flowers
